newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka troops go without cigarettes in north.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka troops go without cigarettes in north.

text.p: Sri Lanka troops battling Tamil Tiger rebels in the north have not received their promised smoke since January because the government has yet to find money to pay tobacco companies, military officials said on Saturday.

Soldiers holding the northern frontline in the war against Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels have not been issued their monthly supply of subsidised cigarettes even though money continues to be deducted from their pay, the Weekend Express newspaper said on Saturday.

It said 212 rupees ($3.6) are deducted from each soldier's monthly salary for payment towards a carton of cigarettes, which costs three times more on the open market. The treasury bears the remaining cost by reimbursing tobacco companies.
"The army commander is working on it," one military official said, referring to finding the money to pay the tobacco companies.
"From December we've been trying to get this allocation from the treasury," the official said.
Sri Lankan troops are battling LTTE rebels in the north after launching a fresh offensive earlier this week.

The LTTE are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
